units.passage: Debugging assistance
units.why: Permitted use "Debugging assistance" (P13) and it is coded under the type that matches the use it names.

units.passage: GenAI is permitted only for specific, instructor-defined tasks (e.g., explaining error messages, suggesting debugging approaches).
units.why: Examples of allowed tasks, 'explaining error messages, suggesting debugging approaches', are P13.

units.passage: AI can be used to help understand code syntax and provide examples. For example, AI coding tools can give examples of CSS rules, which can then be integrated (as appropriate) into coding projects for a class.
units.why: AI may help 'understand code syntax and provide examples'; explaining syntax fits P13 (clarify syntax) more than P12.

units.passage: Use generative AI tools for code completion, debugging, and optimization to enhance performance and efficiency.
units.why: "code completion, debugging, and optimization" are listed as encouraged uses; debugging is the headline use so P13.

units.passage: AI can be a powerful aid in coding, debugging, and conceptual understanding, but it should not be a substitute for personal effort and academic integrity.
units.why: 'debugging' is named as a use where AI is a powerful aid, so AI help in debugging is permitted: P13.

units.passage: seek assistance from official language documentation (e.g. Python.org for Python, Oracle for Java, Linux man-pages for C) to assist in learning syntax and understanding error messages
units.why: Students 'may ... seek assistance from official language documentation ... to assist in learning syntax and understanding error messages'; permitted help for errors and syntax, closest P13 although the source is documentation, not AI.

units.passage: Coding assistance: debugging code you wrote, having AI explain an algorithm or concept, or generating sample code strictly for learning purposes; applies to software code and hardware description and specification languages.
units.why: 'Coding assistance: debugging code you wrote, having AI explain an algorithm or concept, or generating sample code strictly for learning purposes' defines a category: P13.
units.fit_note: A category definition that also covers explaining algorithms and sample code for learning.

units.passage: Debugging Assistance: AI can help identify errors in student code and suggest possible fixes.
units.why: Names AI helping 'identify errors in student code and suggest possible fixes', allowed debugging help (P13).

units.passage: For starting or creating a general/routine structure for coding, and/or debugging your code, so long as the substantial/vast majority (75% or higher, not counting the documentation part) of the code is yours, and that *you* understand, test, and document the code entirely and thoroughly.
units.why: Lists 'debugging your code' as acceptable AI use: P13.
units.fit_note: Also permits AI for starting a routine code structure.

units.passage: Show students how to leverage generative AI as a teaching assistant.
units.policy: Instructors show students how to leverage generative AI as a teaching assistant for questions about code syntax or formatting.
units.why: "Show students how to leverage generative AI as a teaching assistant" for "code syntax or formatting" questions endorses AI help with syntax; P13 (explain errors, clarify syntax) is the nearest.
units.fit_note: Framed as offloading instructor workload; the permission to students is implied.

units.passage: explain error messages; suggest debugging strategies (no final solutions unless allowed).
units.why: Under the tutor category, coding/homework allows 'explain error messages; suggest debugging strategies (no final solutions unless allowed)': P13.

units.passage: debug suggestions; unit-test scaffolds; refactoring ideas you understand.
units.why: Coding/homework allows 'debug suggestions; unit-test scaffolds; refactoring ideas you understand'; help with debugging: P13.

units.passage: GAI can also serve as a valuable tool in data analysis, as well as in the creation and debugging of computer programs, and as such, can lower barriers for including these topics in non-specialist courses.
units.why: Says GAI can serve in "the creation and debugging of computer programs", a statement that AI help with coding and debugging is valuable; P13 fits debugging help, as a rationale (informs).

units.passage: checking your work for errors or getting help to identify a minor error or misunderstanding, so that you can fix those errors on your own.
units.policy: Level 2 allows checking your work for errors or getting help to identify a minor error or misunderstanding, so that you can fix those errors on your own.
units.why: Level 2 allows AI help finding errors if the student fixes them, matching error help (P13).

units.passage: For example, in this course, generative AI tools could be used for * brainstorming and developing ideas that might form the seed for a paper, project, or presentation; * seeking alternative explanations for course content to help you understand the material; * generating text, code, images, videos, and other media that can be used, in whole or in part, in the final submission; * summarizing research sources or complex topics to aid in understanding; * revising writing to improve clarity, grammar, or style; * checking your work for errors or getting help to locate the source of an error or misunderstanding; * translating text from one language to another.
units.why: Level 3 allows AI help locating errors (P13).

units.passage: Use internet/generative AI to figure out errors only if you need it
units.why: ME 208: 'Use internet/generative AI to figure out errors only if you need it' allows AI for errors after trying first, P13.

units.passage: Students may use GenAI to support learning, brainstorming, editing, debugging, or gener- ating explanations, but may not use it to produce full or substantial assignment solutions.
units.policy: Students may use GenAI for debugging.
units.why: B.2 allows GenAI for 'debugging' (P13).

units.passage: For this assignment, you may use AI only to [list permitted purposes, such as generate practice questions, brainstorm alternatives, receive feedback on a student-written draft, or debug student-written code].
units.why: In the Yellow sample, "debug student-written code" is a named permitted use; P13, may.

units.passage: [list of allowed assignments, tasks e.g., idea generation, grammar improvement, coding debugging]
units.why: The template example lists "coding debugging" as allowed, which is AI help with debugging (P13).

units.passage: Using AI to help diagnose error messages.
units.why: 'Using AI to help diagnose error messages' is a listed acceptable use, P13.

units.passage: Troubleshoot code, calculations, data analysis, or technical problems;
units.why: Conditionally permitted: 'Troubleshoot code, calculations, data analysis, or technical problems'; P13.

units.passage: This can be an effective way to more efficiently manage large amounts of Stack Overflow posts
units.why: 'Can I use AI as a Stack Overflow alternative? ... This can be an effective way to more efficiently manage large amounts of Stack Overflow posts' allows AI as a source of programming help, closest to P13 (explain errors and help debug).
units.fit_note: Reconciler: Describes using AI to find and manage programming help posts (a Stack Overflow alternative), not only explaining errors. Coder A: AI as a search alternative for code questions. Coder B: Search-style help for code questions, not specifically error explanation.

units.passage: You ARE allowed to use ChatGPT, Google Bard, Bing AI, or similar AI chatbots as you would a library resource. For example, you can use ChatGPT to find solutions for errors the same way you would use Stackoverflow or other Internet resources, or to understand and improve software you are developing.
units.why: 'You ARE allowed to use ChatGPT ... as you would a library resource ... to find solutions for errors' permits AI for error help and understanding software: P13.

units.passage: Debugging code, checking syntax, or troubleshooting errors (with the expectation that you understand and can explain any code you submit)
units.why: Recommended: "Debugging code, checking syntax, or troubleshooting errors" provided you can explain submitted code, P13.
units.fit_note: Condition: student understands and can explain submitted code. Conditioned on understanding and being able to explain submitted code (P30).

units.passage: and should be limited to debugging or seeking guidance.
units.why: For group activities AI "should be limited to debugging or seeking guidance", a narrow allowed use, P13 (debugging; guidance is not separately typed).
units.fit_note: Also allows seeking guidance, not only debugging.

units.passage: Your code for a programming assignment does not compile. You ask AI to help suggest a bug fix
units.why: The Level 1 example 'You ask AI to help suggest a bug fix' for code that does not compile is permitted debugging help, P13.

units.passage: Debugging code
units.why: 'Debugging code' (with 'Coding assistance') is a listed permitted purpose: P13.
